summary: This section explains how a Producer Company can invest its money, buy shares in other companies, and form subsidiaries. It requires general reserves to be put into safe options like government bonds or fixed deposits to earn good returns. It also sets rules for keeping a proper register of all investments at the office.
points: General reserves must be invested in approved securities, fixed deposits, units, or government and bank bonds for the highest returns.
A Producer Company can buy shares in another Producer Company to promote its goals.
A Producer Company can form a subsidiary or joint venture with any body corporate using a special resolution.
Investments in other companies cannot exceed thirty percent of paid-up capital and free reserves, unless approved by members and the Central Government.
All investments must match the objects of the Producer Company.
The company must keep a register of all investments at its registered office for members to inspect.
example: Meera Producer Company Limited wanted to grow its business by investing its general reserves. The directors decided to put the money into fixed deposits with a scheduled bank to get good returns. Later, to promote its objects, Meera Producer Company Limited passed a special resolution to form a joint venture with a body corporate. The company also bought shares in another company, keeping the total investment within thirty percent of its paid-up capital and free reserves. The manager carefully recorded every detail in an investment register kept at the registered office, which any member could visit and inspect.

terms.meaning: Profits set aside by a company for future use.
A company controlled by another company.
A decision passed by members with a required high majority of votes.
The total amount of money shareholders have paid to the company for shares.

watch: Note that investing beyond the thirty percent limit requires both a special resolution and prior approval from the Central Government.
